label: Engineering
summary: NLM MeSH describes Engineering as: The practical application of physical, mechanical, and mathematical principles. (Stedman, 25th ed)

label: Technology
summary: NLM MeSH describes Technology as: The application of scientific knowledge to practical purposes in any field. It includes methods, techniques, and instrumentation.

label: Bioengineering
summary: NLM MeSH describes Bioengineering as: The application of engineering principles and methods to living organisms or biological systems.

label: Biomedical Engineering
summary: NLM MeSH describes Biomedical Engineering as: Application of principles and practices of engineering science to biomedical research and health care.

label: Chemical Engineering
summary: NLM MeSH describes Chemical Engineering as: Application of principles and practices of engineering science to the transformation, design, and manufacture of substances on an industrial scale.

label: Ergonomics
summary: NLM MeSH describes Ergonomics as: The science of designing, building or equipping mechanical devices or artificial environments to the anthropometric, physiological, or psychological requirements of the people who will use them.

label: Optics and Photonics
summary: NLM MeSH describes Optics and Photonics as: A specialized field of physics and engineering involved in studying the behavior and properties of light and the technology of analyzing, generating, transmitting, and manipulating ELECTROMAGNETIC RADIATION in the visible, infrared, and ultraviolet range.

label: Quality Improvement
summary: NLM MeSH describes Quality Improvement as: The attainment or process of attaining a new level of performance or quality.

label: Sanitary Engineering
summary: NLM MeSH describes Sanitary Engineering as: A branch of engineering concerned with the design, construction, and maintenance of environmental facilities conducive to public health, such as water supply and waste disposal.

label: Culturally Appropriate Technology
summary: NLM MeSH describes Culturally Appropriate Technology as: A SCIENCE or TECHNOLOGY that promotes self-sufficiency and is suitable to the cultural, environmental, economic and social conditions of the geographic area in which it is applied.

label: Automation
summary: NLM MeSH describes Automation as: Controlled operation of an apparatus, process, or system by mechanical or electronic devices that take the place of human organs of observation, effort, and decision. (From Webster's Collegiate Dictionary, 1993)

label: Digital Technology
summary: NLM MeSH describes Digital Technology as: The design and development of devices and procedures that collect, store, analyze, manipulate, and display numerically encoded information, usually via processes encoded in the binary number system.

label: Disruptive Technology
summary: NLM MeSH describes Disruptive Technology as: A process by which a product or service takes root initially in simple applications at the bottom of a market and then relentlessly moves up market, eventually displacing established competitors. (http://www.claytonchristensen.com/key-concepts)

label: Educational Technology
summary: NLM MeSH describes Educational Technology as: Systematic identification, development, organization, or utilization of educational resources and the management of these processes. It is occasionally used also in a more limited sense to describe the use of equipment-oriented techniques or audiovisual aids in educational settings. (Thesaurus of ERIC Descriptors, December 1993, p132)

label: Green Chemistry Technology
summary: NLM MeSH describes Green Chemistry Technology as: Pollution prevention through the design of effective chemical products that have low or no toxicity and use of chemical processes that reduce or eliminate the use and generation of hazardous substances.

label: Haptic Technology
summary: NLM MeSH describes Haptic Technology as: The study of the use of touch and KINESTHESIS in order to produce HAPTIC COMPUTER INTERFACES that will allow users to interact with digital objects by kinesthetic feedback, force feedback, and tactile feedback.

label: Inventions
summary: NLM MeSH describes Inventions as: A novel composition, device, or process, independently conceived de novo or derived from a pre-existing model.

label: Man-Machine Systems
summary: NLM MeSH describes Man-Machine Systems as: A system in which the functions of the man and the machine are interrelated and necessary for the operation of the system.

label: Materials Science
summary: NLM MeSH describes Materials Science as: An interdisciplinary study of the microstructure and composition of various materials such as metals, semiconductors, ceramics, and polymers, in relation to their macromolecular physical and chemical properties. Materials science enables the custom creation of new materials with specific properties and uses.

label: Medical Laboratory Science
summary: NLM MeSH describes Medical Laboratory Science as: The specialty related to the performance of techniques in clinical pathology such as those in hematology, microbiology, and other general clinical laboratory applications.

label: Miniaturization
summary: NLM MeSH describes Miniaturization as: The design or construction of objects greatly reduced in scale.

label: Printing, Three-Dimensional
summary: NLM MeSH describes Printing, Three-Dimensional as: Process for making, building or constructing a physical object from a three-dimensional digital model by laying down many successive thin layers of building material.

label: Quality Control
summary: NLM MeSH describes Quality Control as: A system for verifying and maintaining a desired level of quality in a product or process by careful planning, use of proper equipment, continued inspection, and corrective action as required. (Random House Unabridged Dictionary, 2d ed)

label: Technology, Dental
summary: NLM MeSH describes Technology, Dental as: The field of dentistry involved in procedures for designing and constructing dental appliances. It includes also the application of any technology to the field of dentistry.

label: Technology, Pharmaceutical
summary: NLM MeSH describes Technology, Pharmaceutical as: The application of scientific knowledge or technology to pharmacy and the pharmaceutical industry. It includes methods, techniques, and instrumentation in the manufacture, preparation, compounding, dispensing, packaging, and storing of drugs and other preparations used in diagnostic and determinative procedures, and in the treatment of patients.

label: Technology, Radiologic
summary: NLM MeSH describes Technology, Radiologic as: The application of scientific knowledge or technology to the field of radiology. The applications center mostly around x-ray or radioisotopes for diagnostic and therapeutic purposes but the technological applications of any radiation or radiologic procedure is within the scope of radiologic technology.

label: Technology Transfer
summary: NLM MeSH describes Technology Transfer as: Spread and adoption of inventions and techniques from one geographic area to another, from one discipline to another, or from one sector of the economy to another. For example, improvements in medical equipment may be transferred from industrial countries to developing countries, advances arising from aerospace engineering may be applied to equipment for persons with disabilities, and innovations in science arising from government research are made available to private enterprise.

label: Bioprinting
summary: NLM MeSH describes Bioprinting as: A material transfer technique used for assembling biological material or cells into a prescribed organization to create functional structures such as MICROCHIP ANALYTICAL DEVICES , cell microarrays, or three dimensional anatomical structures.

label: Cell Engineering
summary: NLM MeSH describes Cell Engineering as: Methods and techniques used to modify or select cells and develop conditions for growing cells for biosynthetic production of molecules ( METABOLIC ENGINEERING ), for generation of tissue structures and organs in vitro ( TISSUE ENGINEERING ), or for other BIOENGINEERING research objectives.

label: Synthetic Biology
summary: NLM MeSH describes Synthetic Biology as: A field of biological research combining engineering in the formulation, design, and building (synthesis) of novel biological structures, functions, and systems.

label: Eye-Tracking Technology
summary: NLM MeSH describes Eye-Tracking Technology as: Technology used for EYE MOVEMENT MEASUREMENTS , which capture and measure a persons EYE MOVEMENT and/or EYE GAZE

label: Water Supply
summary: NLM MeSH describes Water Supply as: Means or process of supplying water (as for a community) usually including reservoirs, tunnels, and pipelines and often the watershed from which the water is ultimately drawn. (Webster, 3d ed)

label: User-Centered Design
summary: NLM MeSH describes User-Centered Design as: Design process using input from users regarding systems, devices, or software.

label: Automation, Laboratory
summary: NLM MeSH describes Automation, Laboratory as: Controlled operations of analytic or diagnostic processes, or systems by mechanical or electronic devices.

label: Multiple-Instance Learning Algorithms
summary: NLM MeSH describes Multiple-Instance Learning Algorithms as: Weakly supervised learning algorithms where training set is arranged in a labeled bag of instances, and a single class label is assigned to a bag.

label: Robotics
summary: NLM MeSH describes Robotics as: The application of electronic, computerized control systems to mechanical devices designed to perform human functions. Formerly restricted to industry, but nowadays applied to artificial organs controlled by bionic (bioelectronic) devices, like automated insulin pumps and other prostheses.

label: Biomedical Technology
summary: NLM MeSH describes Biomedical Technology as: The application of technology to the solution of medical problems.

label: Biomimetics
summary: NLM MeSH describes Biomimetics as: An interdisciplinary field in materials science, ENGINEERING , and BIOLOGY , studying the use of biological principles for synthesis or fabrication of BIOMIMETIC MATERIALS .

label: Bioreactors
summary: NLM MeSH describes Bioreactors as: Tools or devices for generating products using the synthetic or chemical conversion capacity of a biological system. They can be classical fermentors, cell culture perfusion systems, or enzyme bioreactors. For production of proteins or enzymes, recombinant microorganisms such as bacteria, mammalian cells, or insect or plant cells are usually chosen.

label: Industrial Microbiology
summary: NLM MeSH describes Industrial Microbiology as: The study, utilization, and manipulation of those microorganisms capable of economically producing desirable substances or changes in substances, and the control of undesirable microorganisms.

label: Audiovisual Aids
summary: NLM MeSH describes Audiovisual Aids as: Auditory and visual instructional materials.

label: Hot Melt Extrusion Technology
summary: NLM MeSH describes Hot Melt Extrusion Technology as: Solvent-free method for preparing numerous types of drug delivery systems and dosage forms for active pharmaceutical ingredients that have solubility issues. It involves pumping polymeric materials at temperatures above their glass transition temperature to mix in active pharmaceutical ingredients with or without binders thus forming an amorphous product with an increase in the dissolution profile for the active pharmaceutical ingredients.

label: Microtechnology
summary: NLM MeSH describes Microtechnology as: Manufacturing technology for making microscopic devices in the micrometer range (typically 1-100 micrometers), such as integrated circuits or MEMS . The process usually involves replication and parallel fabrication of hundreds or millions of identical structures using various thin film deposition techniques and carried out in environmentally-controlled clean rooms.

label: Stereolithography
summary: NLM MeSH describes Stereolithography as: A 3D printing technology where a computer-controlled moving laser beam is used to build up the required structure, layer by layer, from liquid POLYMERS that harden on contact with laser light (photopolymerization).

label: Laboratory Proficiency Testing
summary: NLM MeSH describes Laboratory Proficiency Testing as: Assessments aimed at determining agreement in diagnostic test results among laboratories. Identical survey samples are distributed to participating laboratories, with results stratified according to testing methodologies.

label: Chemistry Techniques, Synthetic
summary: NLM MeSH describes Chemistry Techniques, Synthetic as: Methods used for the chemical synthesis of compounds. Included under this heading are laboratory methods used to synthesize a variety of chemicals and drugs.

label: Molecular Farming
summary: NLM MeSH describes Molecular Farming as: The large scale production of pharmaceutically important and commercially valuable RECOMBINANT PROTEINS .

label: Metabolic Engineering
summary: NLM MeSH describes Metabolic Engineering as: Methods and techniques used to genetically modify cells' biosynthetic product output and develop conditions for growing the cells as BIOREACTORS .

label: Water Wells
summary: NLM MeSH describes Water Wells as: Constructions built to access underground water.

label: Autonomous Robots
summary: NLM MeSH describes Autonomous Robots as: Machines that are engineered to learn about their environment and make decisions to complete tasks with little to no human intervention. These robots may be designed to complete tasks such as patient intervention, remote monitoring, inventory transportation, among many others.

label: Robotic Surgical Procedures
summary: NLM MeSH describes Robotic Surgical Procedures as: Surgical procedures performed remotely using a computer that controls surgical instruments attached to mechanical arms designed to perform the tasks of the surgeon.

label: Biomedical Enhancement
summary: NLM MeSH describes Biomedical Enhancement as: The use of technology-based interventions to improve functional capacities rather than to treat disease.

label: Nanomedicine
summary: NLM MeSH describes Nanomedicine as: The branch of medicine concerned with the application of NANOTECHNOLOGY to the prevention and treatment of disease. It involves the monitoring, repair, construction, and control of human biological systems at the molecular level, using engineered nanodevices and NANOSTRUCTURES . (From Freitas Jr., Nanomedicine, vol 1, 1999).

label: Photobioreactors
summary: NLM MeSH describes Photobioreactors as: Devices for generating biological products that use light as the energy source. They are used for controlled BIOMASS production such as growing cyanobacteria, mosses, or algae.

label: Books, Illustrated
summary: NLM MeSH describes Books, Illustrated as: Books containing photographs, prints, drawings, portraits, plates, diagrams, facsimiles, maps, tables, or other representations or systematic arrangement of data designed to elucidate or decorate its contents. (From The ALA Glossary of Library and Information Science, 1983, p114)

label: Models, Structural
summary: NLM MeSH describes Models, Structural as: A representation, generally small in scale, to show the structure, construction, or appearance of something. (From Random House Unabridged Dictionary, 2d ed)

label: Motion Pictures
summary: NLM MeSH describes Motion Pictures as: The art, technique, or business of producing motion pictures for entertainment, propaganda, or instruction.

label: Multimedia
summary: NLM MeSH describes Multimedia as: Materials, frequently computer applications, that combine some or all of text, sound, graphics, animation, and video into integrated packages. (Thesaurus of ERIC Descriptors, 1994)

label: Optical Storage Devices
summary: NLM MeSH describes Optical Storage Devices as: A computer disk read by a laser beam, containing data prerecorded by a vendor. The buyer cannot enter or modify data in any way but the advantages lie in the speed of accessibility, relative immunity to damage, and relatively low cost of purchase.

label: Radio
summary: NLM MeSH describes Radio as: The transmission and reception of electric impulses or signals by means of electric waves without a connecting wire, or the use of these waves for the wireless transmission of electric impulses into which sound is converted. (From Webster's 3d)

label: Sound Recordings
summary: NLM MeSH describes Sound Recordings as: The storing of sound signals on various media such as cylinders, analog discs, digital discs, tapes, and wires.[LCSH, 10/27/2020]

label: Tape Recording
summary: NLM MeSH describes Tape Recording as: Recording of information on magnetic or punched paper tape.

label: Television
summary: NLM MeSH describes Television as: The transmission and reproduction of transient images of fixed or moving objects. An electronic system of transmitting such images together with sound over a wire or through space by apparatus that converts light and sound into electrical waves and reconverts them into visible light rays and audible sound. (From Webster, 3rd ed)

label: Microfluidics
summary: NLM MeSH describes Microfluidics as: The study of fluid channels and chambers of tiny dimensions of tens to hundreds of micrometers and volumes of nanoliters or picoliters. This is of interest in biological MICROCIRCULATION and used in MICROCHEMISTRY and INVESTIGATIVE TECHNIQUES .

label: Click Chemistry
summary: NLM MeSH describes Click Chemistry as: Organic chemistry methodology that mimics the modular nature of various biosynthetic processes. It uses highly reliable and selective reactions designed to click i.e., rapidly join small modular units together in high yield, without offensive byproducts. In combination with COMBINATORIAL CHEMISTRY TECHNIQUES , it is used for the synthesis of new compounds and combinatorial libraries.

label: Combinatorial Chemistry Techniques
summary: NLM MeSH describes Combinatorial Chemistry Techniques as: A technology, in which sets of reactions for solution or solid-phase synthesis, is used to create molecular libraries for analysis of compounds on a large scale.

label: Cycloaddition Reaction
summary: NLM MeSH describes Cycloaddition Reaction as: Synthetic organic reactions that use reactions between unsaturated molecules to form cyclical products.

label: Molecular Imprinting
summary: NLM MeSH describes Molecular Imprinting as: A methodology for chemically synthesizing polymer molds of specific molecules or recognition sites of specific molecules. Applications for MOLECULARLY IMPRINTED POLYMERS (MIPs) include separations, assays and biosensors, and catalysis.

label: Solid-Phase Synthesis Techniques
summary: NLM MeSH describes Solid-Phase Synthesis Techniques as: Techniques used to synthesize chemicals using molecular substrates that are bound to a solid surface. Typically a series of reactions are conducted on the bound substrate that results in either the covalent attachment of specific moieties or the modification of existing function groups. These techniques offer an advantage to those involving solution reactions in that the substrate compound does not have to be isolated and purified between the reaction steps.

label: Genetic Enhancement
summary: NLM MeSH describes Genetic Enhancement as: The use of genetic methodologies to improve functional capacities of an organism rather than to treat disease.

label: Models, Anatomic
summary: NLM MeSH describes Models, Anatomic as: Three-dimensional representation to show anatomic structures. Models may be used in place of intact animals or organisms for teaching, practice, and study.

label: Videodisc Recording
summary: NLM MeSH describes Videodisc Recording as: The storing of visual and usually sound signals on discs for later reproduction on a television screen or monitor.

label: Videotape Recording
summary: NLM MeSH describes Videotape Recording as: Recording of visual and sometimes sound signals on magnetic tape.

label: Microscopy, Video
summary: NLM MeSH describes Microscopy, Video as: Microscopy in which television cameras are used to brighten magnified images that are otherwise too dark to be seen with the naked eye. It is used frequently in TELEPATHOLOGY .

label: SELEX Aptamer Technique
summary: NLM MeSH describes SELEX Aptamer Technique as: A method of generating a large library of randomized nucleotides and selecting NUCLEOTIDE APTAMERS by iterative rounds of in vitro selection. A modified procedure substitutes AMINO ACIDS in place of NUCLEOTIDES to make PEPTIDE APTAMERS .

label: Causality
summary: NLM MeSH describes Causality as: The relating of causes to the effects they produce. Causes are termed necessary when they must always precede an effect and sufficient when they initiate or produce an effect. Any of several factors may be associated with the potential disease causation or outcome, including predisposing factors, enabling factors, precipitating factors, reinforcing factors, and risk factors.

label: Research Design
summary: NLM MeSH describes Research Design as: A plan for collecting and utilizing data so that desired information can be obtained with sufficient precision or so that an hypothesis can be tested properly.

label: Science
summary: NLM MeSH describes Science as: The study of natural phenomena by observation, measurement, and experimentation.

label: Precipitating Factors
summary: NLM MeSH describes Precipitating Factors as: Factors associated with the definitive onset of a disease, illness, accident, behavioral response, or course of action. Usually one factor is more important or more obviously recognizable than others, if several are involved, and one may often be regarded as necessary. Examples include exposure to specific disease; amount or level of an infectious organism, drug, or noxious agent, etc.

label: Protective Factors
summary: NLM MeSH describes Protective Factors as: An aspect of personal behavior or lifestyle, environmental exposure, or inborn or inherited characteristic, which, on the basis of epidemiologic evidence, is known to be associated with prevention or mitigation of a health-related condition considered important to prevent.

label: Risk Factors
summary: NLM MeSH describes Risk Factors as: An aspect of personal behavior or lifestyle, environmental exposure, inborn or inherited characteristic, which, based on epidemiological evidence, is known to be associated with a health-related condition considered important to prevent.

label: Control Groups
summary: NLM MeSH describes Control Groups as: Groups that serve as a standard for comparison in experimental studies. They are similar in relevant characteristics to the experimental group but do not receive the experimental intervention.

label: Double-Blind Method
summary: NLM MeSH describes Double-Blind Method as: A method of studying a drug or procedure in which both the subjects and investigators are kept unaware of who is actually getting which specific treatment.

label: Random Allocation
summary: NLM MeSH describes Random Allocation as: A process involving chance used in therapeutic trials or other research endeavor for allocating experimental subjects, human or animal, between treatment and control groups, or among treatment groups. It may also apply to experiments on inanimate objects.

label: Sample Size
summary: NLM MeSH describes Sample Size as: The number of units (persons, animals, patients, specified circumstances, etc.) in a population to be studied. The sample size should be big enough to have a high likelihood of detecting a true difference between two groups. (From Wassertheil-Smoller, Biostatistics and Epidemiology, 1990, p95)

label: Research
summary: NLM MeSH describes Research as: Critical and exhaustive investigation or experimentation, having for its aim the discovery of new facts and their correct interpretation, the revision of accepted conclusions, theories, or laws in the light of newly discovered facts, or the practical application of such new or revised conclusions, theories, or laws. (Webster, 3d ed)

label: Systems Integration
summary: NLM MeSH describes Systems Integration as: The procedures involved in combining separately developed modules, components, or subsystems so that they work together as a complete system. (From McGraw-Hill Dictionary of Scientific and Technical Terms, 4th ed)

label: Systems Theory
summary: NLM MeSH describes Systems Theory as: Principles, models, and laws that apply to complex interrelationships and interdependencies of sets of linked components which form a functioning whole, a system. Any system may be composed of components which are systems in their own right (sub-systems), such as several organs within an individual organism.

label: Artificial Life
summary: NLM MeSH describes Artificial Life as: Research involving the synthesis of life and life-like phenomena and the application of such techniques toward the enhancement of our theoretical understanding of life and life-like phenomena, studied through the use of computer programs.

label: Behavioral Research
summary: NLM MeSH describes Behavioral Research as: Research that involves the application of the behavioral and social sciences to the study of the actions or reactions of persons or animals in response to external or internal stimuli. (from American Heritage Dictionary, 4th ed)

label: Biomedical Research
summary: NLM MeSH describes Biomedical Research as: Research that involves the application of the natural sciences, especially biology and physiology, to medicine.

label: Community-Based Participatory Research
summary: NLM MeSH describes Community-Based Participatory Research as: Collaborative process of research involving researchers and community representatives.

label: Empirical Research
summary: NLM MeSH describes Empirical Research as: The study, based on direct observation, use of statistical records, interviews, or experimental methods, of actual practices or the actual impact of practices or policies.

label: Evidence Gaps
summary: NLM MeSH describes Evidence Gaps as: Areas where little or no evidence from impact evaluations and SYSTEMATIC REVIEWS is available and where future research should be focused (from https://openknowledge.worldbank.org/handle/10986/16941).

label: Interdisciplinary Research
summary: NLM MeSH describes Interdisciplinary Research as: Research combining mastery in distinct fields or disciplines that apply and exchange tools, concepts, ideas, data methods, or results around a common project.

label: Knowledge Discovery
summary: NLM MeSH describes Knowledge Discovery as: A process that searches for hidden and important connections among information or results.

label: Operations Research
summary: NLM MeSH describes Operations Research as: A group of techniques developed to apply scientific methods and tools to solve the problems of DECISION MAKING in complex organizations and systems. Operations research searches for optimal solutions in situations of conflicting GOALS and makes use of mathematical models from which solutions for actual problems may be derived. (From Psychiatric Dictionary, 6th ed)

label: Peer Review, Research
summary: NLM MeSH describes Peer Review, Research as: The evaluation by experts of the quality and pertinence of research or research proposals of other experts in the same field. Peer review is used by editors in deciding which submissions warrant publication, by granting agencies to determine which proposals should be funded, and by academic institutions in tenure decisions.

label: Proof of Concept Study
summary: NLM MeSH describes Proof of Concept Study as: An empirical investigation which pertains to the development of prototypes or models that demonstrate the feasibility of novel concepts, ideas, principles, schema or their practical application.

label: Research Report
summary: NLM MeSH describes Research Report as: Detailed account or statement or formal record of data resulting from empirical inquiry.

label: Social Validity, Research
summary: NLM MeSH describes Social Validity, Research as: Evaluation of the degree of acceptance for the immediate variables associated with a procedure or program designed to change behavior. This includes the social significance of the goals of treatment, the social appropriateness of the treatment procedures, and the social importance of the effects of treatments.

label: Biobehavioral Sciences
summary: NLM MeSH describes Biobehavioral Sciences as: An interdisciplinary scientific approach to the study of complex interactions among biological, social, behavioral and environmental factors.

label: Embryo Research
summary: NLM MeSH describes Embryo Research as: Experimentation on, or using the organs or tissues from, a human or other mammalian conceptus during the prenatal stage of development that is characterized by rapid morphological changes and the differentiation of basic structures. In humans, this includes the period from the time of fertilization to the end of the eighth week after fertilization.

label: Fetal Research
summary: NLM MeSH describes Fetal Research as: Experimentation on, or using the organs or tissues from, a human or other mammalian conceptus in the postembryonic period, after the major structures have been outlined. In humans, this corresponds to the period from the third month after fertilization until birth.

label: Genetic Research
summary: NLM MeSH describes Genetic Research as: Research into the cause, transmission, amelioration, elimination, or enhancement of inherited disorders and traits.

label: Health Services Research
summary: NLM MeSH describes Health Services Research as: The integration of epidemiologic, sociological, economic, and other analytic sciences in the study of health services. Health services research is usually concerned with relationships between need, demand, supply, use, and outcome of health services. The aim of the research is evaluation, particularly in terms of structure, process, output, and outcome. (From Last, Dictionary of Epidemiology, 2d ed)

label: Human Experimentation
summary: NLM MeSH describes Human Experimentation as: The use of humans as investigational subjects.

label: Outcome Assessment, Health Care
summary: NLM MeSH describes Outcome Assessment, Health Care as: Research aimed at assessing the quality and effectiveness of health care as measured by the attainment of a specified end result or outcome. Measures include parameters such as improved health, lowered morbidity or mortality, and improvement of abnormal states (such as elevated blood pressure).

label: Pharmaceutical Research
summary: NLM MeSH describes Pharmaceutical Research as: RESEARCH activity focused on pharmaceutical products and services.

label: Pharmacy Research
summary: NLM MeSH describes Pharmacy Research as: RESEARCH activity focused on PHARMACY .

label: Rehabilitation Research
summary: NLM MeSH describes Rehabilitation Research as: Studies and research concerning the psychological, educational, social, vocational, industrial, and economic aspects of REHABILITATION .

label: Stem Cell Research
summary: NLM MeSH describes Stem Cell Research as: Experimentation on STEM CELLS and on the use of stem cells.

label: Translational Research, Biomedical
summary: NLM MeSH describes Translational Research, Biomedical as: The endeavour to traverse a specific step of the translation process of turning an observation in the laboratory, clinic, or community into an intervention that will improve the health of individuals and the public. (from Nat Rev Drug Discov. 2018 July ; 17(7): 455–456.)

label: Citizen Science
summary: NLM MeSH describes Citizen Science as: Voluntary public participation in the scientific process, addressing real-world problems in ways that may include formulating research questions, conducting scientific experiments, collecting and analyzing data, interpreting results, making new discoveries, developing technologies and applications, for solving complex problems. (From https://www.citizenscience.gov/)

label: Grounded Theory
summary: NLM MeSH describes Grounded Theory as: The generation of theories from analysis of empirical data.

label: Qualitative Research
summary: NLM MeSH describes Qualitative Research as: Any type of research that employs nonnumeric information to explore individual or group characteristics, producing findings not arrived at by statistical procedures or other quantitative means. (Qualitative Inquiry: A Dictionary of Terms Thousand Oaks, CA: Sage Publications, 1997)

label: Mathematics
summary: NLM MeSH describes Mathematics as: The deductive study of shape, quantity, and dependence. (From McGraw-Hill Dictionary of Scientific and Technical Terms, 6th ed)

label: Probability
summary: NLM MeSH describes Probability as: The study of chance processes or the relative frequency characterizing a chance process.

label: Models, Statistical
summary: NLM MeSH describes Models, Statistical as: Statistical formulations or analyses which, when applied to data and found to fit the data, are then used to verify the assumptions and parameters used in the analysis. Examples of statistical models are the linear model, binomial model, polynomial model, two-parameter model, etc.

label: Data Analysis
summary: NLM MeSH describes Data Analysis as: Process of systematically applying statistical and/or logical techniques to describe and illustrate, condense and recap, and evaluate data (https://ori.hhs.gov/education).

label: Nonlinear Dynamics
summary: NLM MeSH describes Nonlinear Dynamics as: The study of systems which respond disproportionately (nonlinearly) to initial conditions or perturbing stimuli. Nonlinear systems may exhibit chaos which is classically characterized as sensitive dependence on initial conditions. Chaotic systems, while distinguished from more ordered periodic systems, are not random. When their behavior over time is appropriately displayed (in phase space), constraints are evident which are described by strange attractors. Phase space representations of chaotic systems, or strange attractors, usually reveal fractal ( FRACTALS ) self-similarity across time scales. Natural, including biological, systems often display nonlinear dynamics and chaos.

label: Bayes Theorem
summary: NLM MeSH describes Bayes Theorem as: A theorem in probability theory named for Thomas Bayes (1702-1761). In epidemiology, it is used to obtain the probability of disease in a group of people with some characteristic on the basis of the overall rate of that disease and of the likelihood of that characteristic in healthy and diseased individuals. The most familiar application is in clinical decision analysis where it is used for estimating the probability of a particular diagnosis given the appearance of some symptoms or test result.

label: Likelihood Functions
summary: NLM MeSH describes Likelihood Functions as: Functions constructed from a statistical model and a set of observed data which give the probability of that data for various values of the unknown model parameters. Those parameter values that maximize the probability are the maximum likelihood estimates of the parameters.

label: Risk
summary: NLM MeSH describes Risk as: The probability that an event will occur. It encompasses a variety of measures of the probability of a generally unfavorable outcome.

label: Uncertainty
summary: NLM MeSH describes Uncertainty as: The condition in which reasonable knowledge regarding risks, benefits, or the future is not available.

label: Linear Models
summary: NLM MeSH describes Linear Models as: Statistical models in which the value of a parameter for a given value of a factor is assumed to be equal to a + bx, where a and b are constants. The models predict a linear regression.

label: Logistic Models
summary: NLM MeSH describes Logistic Models as: Statistical models which describe the relationship between a qualitative dependent variable (that is, one which can take only certain discrete values, such as the presence or absence of a disease) and an independent variable. A common application is in epidemiology for estimating an individual's risk (probability of a disease) as a function of a given risk factor.

label: Models, Spatial Interaction
summary: NLM MeSH describes Models, Spatial Interaction as: Estimates of the flow of people, material or information between locations in geographic space.

label: Autoencoder
summary: NLM MeSH describes Autoencoder as: An unsupervised learning technique where the machine learns patterns in unlabeled data sets, makes compressed representations and reconstructs the input as output at minimum loss of features from the input. Autoencoders are useful in denoising images, DIMENSIONALITY REDUCTION and feature extraction.

label: Backtracking Algorithms
summary: NLM MeSH describes Backtracking Algorithms as: A general algorithmic technique that considers solutions one option at a time backtracking to get the desired solution. This allows searching every possible option recursively.

label: Boosting Machine Learning Algorithms
summary: NLM MeSH describes Boosting Machine Learning Algorithms as: A form of ensemble learning methods which combines weak learners to create strong ones, which reduces training errors and bias in the training models. There are different types of boosting such as gradient boosting, XGBoost, and Adaboost.

label: Clustering Algorithms
summary: NLM MeSH describes Clustering Algorithms as: Algorithms designed to find groups of similar data points (called clusters) in the dataset. Clustering is often used for feature engineering or pattern discovery in unsupervised machine learning.

label: Compression Algorithms
summary: NLM MeSH describes Compression Algorithms as: A class of algorithms which both reduces and restores the size of files to increase their portability. Compression algorithms can be lossy or lossless.

label: Detection Algorithms
summary: NLM MeSH describes Detection Algorithms as: Algorithms designed to find or localize the objects in images and assign the objects (affordances).

label: Dimensionality Reduction
summary: NLM MeSH describes Dimensionality Reduction as: A machine learning process used to reduce the number of attributes or features of data (called dimensionality) thereby simplifying understanding of the dataset without a loss in data integrity.

label: Genetic Algorithms
summary: NLM MeSH describes Genetic Algorithms as: Heuristic search algorithms which direct the random searches to the area of better performance or fitness function by computationally creating the conditions inspired by NATURAL SELECTION . They are commonly used to generate solutions for optimization problems.

label: Latent Class Analysis
summary: NLM MeSH describes Latent Class Analysis as: A statistical algorithm used to analyze clusters of observed variables by constructing categorical unobserved or latent segment based on weighted analysis and the average probabilities. Such latent classes are used to infer variables whose relationships are not directly observed. In biomedical research, it is often used to categorize data that allows the determination of symptom clusters.

label: Machine Learning Algorithms
summary: NLM MeSH describes Machine Learning Algorithms as: A class of algorithms which enables a computer to learn as it goes, thereby accomplishing its goal without being explicitly programmed to do so.

label: Parallel Algorithms
summary: NLM MeSH describes Parallel Algorithms as: Algorithms that can execute several instructions simultaneously on different processing devices and then combine all the individual outputs to produce the final result.

label: Particle Swarm Optimization
summary: NLM MeSH describes Particle Swarm Optimization as: A heuristic computational algorithm designed to find optimal solutions in a random search space. Particle swarm optimization measures swarm intelligence which is a computation measurement inspired by behaviors of self-organized swarming animals.

label: Prediction Algorithms
summary: NLM MeSH describes Prediction Algorithms as: A class of algorithms which are designed to forecast unseen data. Prediction Algorithms can discover patterns, perform classification tasks, and identify trends.

label: Cellular Automata
summary: NLM MeSH describes Cellular Automata as: Space-oriented dynamic modeling ALGORITHMS acting in an array of cells, whose temporal states evolve based on the rules (algorithms) of the automata. They are used to model complex dynamic systems for study and analysis in a variety of scientific fields.

label: Correlation of Data
summary: NLM MeSH describes Correlation of Data as: Determination of whether or not two variables are correlated. This means to study whether an increase or decrease in one variable corresponds to an increase or decrease in the other variable.

label: Intelligent Systems
summary: NLM MeSH describes Intelligent Systems as: Technological systems that perform automated tasks within specific environments enabled by artificial intelligence.

label: Machine Learning
summary: NLM MeSH describes Machine Learning as: A type of ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE that enable COMPUTERS to independently initiate and execute LEARNING when exposed to new data.

label: Pattern Analysis, Machine
summary: NLM MeSH describes Pattern Analysis, Machine as: The process of recognizing and extracting meaningful information from patterns in data. Pattern analysis in machine learning is often used for predictions and forecasting.

label: Prediction Methods, Machine
summary: NLM MeSH describes Prediction Methods, Machine as: Methods of making prediction about a new measurement based on calculations of previous data.

label: Sentiment Analysis
summary: NLM MeSH describes Sentiment Analysis as: A data mining technique in which subjective information such as sentiments, OPINIONS , and attitudes are extracted and analyzed from data.

label: Multifactor Dimensionality Reduction
summary: NLM MeSH describes Multifactor Dimensionality Reduction as: A statistical tool for detecting and modeling gene-gene interactions. It is a non-parametric and model-free approach.

label: Adaptive Algorithms
summary: NLM MeSH describes Adaptive Algorithms as: Algorithms designed to solve a problem by modifying their behaviors when faced with an unseen task with limited data during training.

label: Classification Algorithms
summary: NLM MeSH describes Classification Algorithms as: A class of algorithms that predicts into which category an observation belongs based on training data.

label: Generative Adversarial Networks
summary: NLM MeSH describes Generative Adversarial Networks as: An unsupervised learning network which is composed of two separate networks, a generator which produces content and a discriminator which works to identify real content from the generated content. Over time, generative adversarial networks create data that increasingly resembles the input data.

label: Adverse Outcome Pathways
summary: NLM MeSH describes Adverse Outcome Pathways as: Models connecting initiating events at the cellular and molecular level to population-wide impacts. Computational models may be at levels relating toxicology to adverse effects.

label: Healthcare Failure Mode and Effect Analysis
summary: NLM MeSH describes Healthcare Failure Mode and Effect Analysis as: Prospective risk assessment tool aimed at identifying potential risks and their impact in healthcare settings.

label: Genetic Risk Score
summary: NLM MeSH describes Genetic Risk Score as: Estimate of an individual's genetic liability to a trait or disease, calculated according to their genotype profile and relevant genome-wide association study data. (from Tutorial: a guide to performing polygenic risk score analyses. Nat Protoc. 2020 Sep;15(9):2759.)

label: Heart Disease Risk Factors
summary: NLM MeSH describes Heart Disease Risk Factors as: Aspects of personal behavior or lifestyle, environmental exposure, inherited conditions and characteristics, which are determined to be associated with HEART DISEASES .

label: Deep Learning
summary: NLM MeSH describes Deep Learning as: Supervised or unsupervised machine learning methods that use multiple layers of data representations generated by nonlinear transformations, instead of individual task-specific ALGORITHMS , to build and train neural network models.

label: Ensemble Learning
summary: NLM MeSH describes Ensemble Learning as: A method in machine learning where several base learners are combined to create an optimal learning model. This can be used for a variety of models including forecasting, classification, or function approximation.

label: Federated Learning
summary: NLM MeSH describes Federated Learning as: A method of training machine learning models whereby multiple devices train their own copy of the artificial intelligence model using decentralized local data. These locally trained model results are then aggregated by a central server to update the global model without accessing local data.

label: Reinforcement Machine Learning
summary: NLM MeSH describes Reinforcement Machine Learning as: A machine learning training method in which an agent in an uncertain environment is rewarded for optimal behaviors and punished for undesired behaviors, allowing the agent to learn from trial-and-error.

label: Representation Machine Learning
summary: NLM MeSH describes Representation Machine Learning as: A class of machine learning approaches that allow a system to discover the representations required for feature detection or classification from raw data. The requirement for manual feature engineering is reduced by allowing a machine to learn the features and apply them to a given activity.

label: Supervised Machine Learning
summary: NLM MeSH describes Supervised Machine Learning as: A MACHINE LEARNING paradigm used to make predictions about future instances based on a given set of labeled paired input-output training (sample) data.

label: Transfer Machine Learning
summary: NLM MeSH describes Transfer Machine Learning as: Process of training a new learning network by beginning with previously trained for a related problem, leading to less time and energy required for training the new learning network.

label: Unsupervised Machine Learning
summary: NLM MeSH describes Unsupervised Machine Learning as: A MACHINE LEARNING paradigm used to make predictions about future instances based on a given set of unlabeled paired input-output training (sample) data.

label: Predictive Learning Models
summary: NLM MeSH describes Predictive Learning Models as: Machine learning models which are trained to analyze historical data to find patterns and trends, allowing it to predict future outcomes.

label: Cardiometabolic Risk Factors
summary: NLM MeSH describes Cardiometabolic Risk Factors as: A cluster of personal behavior or lifestyle, environmental exposure, inborn or inherited conditions and characteristics, which, on the basis of epidemiological evidence, is known to be associated with CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASES and TYPE 2 DIABETES MELLITUS .

label: Obesity Paradox
summary: NLM MeSH describes Obesity Paradox as: An observation that high BODY MASS INDEX is sometimes associated with lower CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE mortality in certain population, e.g., ELDERLY .

label: Large Language Models
summary: NLM MeSH describes Large Language Models as: Computational designs that apply DEEP LEARNING methods on extremely large data sets as a basis for predicting and constructing natural-sounding text.

label: Support Vector Machine
summary: NLM MeSH describes Support Vector Machine as: SUPERVISED MACHINE LEARNING algorithm which learns to assign labels to objects from a set of training examples. Examples are learning to recognize fraudulent credit card activity by examining hundreds or thousands of fraudulent and non-fraudulent credit card activity, or learning to make disease diagnosis or prognosis based on automatic classification of microarray gene expression profiles drawn from hundreds or thousands of samples.
